text:
sam_support: FYI ACME onboards reported sudden 403s + TLS failures after our egress IP rotation around 2026-03-16 22:12 UTC. They said services that were previously whitelisted are now blocked.

mike_oncall: Can you paste a sample error and timeframe? Need reproducible evidence to hand to networking.

sam_support: Customer provided this curl output from their side (they ran it at 22:16 UTC):

```
$ curl -v https://api.acme.example/health
* Connected to api.acme.example (35.200.100.7) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.acme.example
> User-Agent: curl/8.0
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< content-length: 58
{"error":"access_denied","reason":"source IP not allowed"}
```

sam_support: They also shared a packet-snippet showing TLS alerts: "TLS alert (level: fatal, description: handshake_failure)" for some sessions, and said some requests succeeded and some failed within the same minute.

leo_network: Sounds like egress source IP is changing mid-session or for different requests. Could be SNAT flapping across our NAT gateways/pools. Which egress pool did we rotate?

sam_support: Per our change log we rotated EU egress pools at 22:10 UTC, moving customers onto new /29 blocks from 35.200.100.0/29 -> 35.200.101.0/29 (rolling swap). ACME had previously allowed-list 35.200.100.5 only.

leo_network: That explains it — if some flows still use .100.5 and new ones use .101.x they'll get blocked. Asking for flow logs.

tara_sre: Please share VPC flow logs for the customer-facing nodes and NAT allocation logs for 22:00-22:30 UTC. We need to see if ephemeral SNAT allocation produced different source IPs for requests from the same client.

sam_support: Pasted trimmed flow log snippet from 22:14:25-22:14:55 UTC (customer IP masked):

```
src=10.12.34.56 dst=api.acme.example src_port=45412 dst_port=443 src_egress=35.200.100.5 action=ACCEPT
src=10.12.34.56 dst=api.acme.example src_port=45414 dst_port=443 src_egress=35.200.101.6 action=REJECT reason=ACL
src=10.12.34.56 dst=api.acme.example src_port=45416 dst_port=443 src_egress=35.200.101.7 action=REJECT reason=ACL
```

sam_support: Customer says they saw successful and failed requests within 10s.

mike_oncall: Yep that's the pattern. Two different SNATs used for nearby connections. Could be our NAT allocator cycling outbound IPs per-connection instead of per-host.

leo_network: I'm checking allocator logs: we had a bug in the egress-rotation daemon that races on release; when node A and B handle bursts we can end up assigning different IPs for the same pod's ephemeral connections. Patch candidate available.

tara_sre: Short-term mitigation — we can pin ACME to a stable egress IP while we deploy the fix. Options:
- create a customer-specific SNAT mapping (single IP)
- ask ACME to update their allowlist to include the entire /29 (but they may be slow)

mike_oncall: Agree. Which is faster?

leo_network: We can create mapping now. Command: 
```
redwoodctl nat assign --customer acme --ip 35.200.101.7 --region eu-west1 --ttl 48h
```
This will sticky NAT ACME flows to .101.7 for the TTL.

sam_support: I'll ask ACME to accept a temporary IP and confirm they'll add the /29 if needed.

deploy-bot: NAT mapping created: acme -> 35.200.101.7 (id: nat-map-4321), expires 48h. Change by leo_network.

sam_support: ACME confirmed they allowed 35.200.101.7 and reran their tests. They sent this curl: 

```
curl -H 'Host: api.acme.example' --resolve api.acme.example:443:35.200.101.7 https://api.acme.example/health -v
* Connected to api.acme.example (35.200.101.7) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.acme.example
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok"}
```

sam_support: They reported immediate improvement.

leo_network: I'll push the allocator race fix to staging and then to prod with a canary. The fix ensures per-source sticky SNAT (per pod) instead of per-connection allocation during rotation.

tara_sre: Long-term we should: update runbook to notify customers 30m before egress rotations, publish egress range in the console per-region, and add a test to detect IP churn for long-lived sessions.

mike_oncall: Created incident ticket INC-2026-349 (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-349) — status: mitigated (customer pinned), next: deploy fix + runbook updates.

sam_support: Marking this thread resolved for now. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

leo_network: Will follow up when fix is rolled.

tara_sre: Add to postmortem if rotation caused customer-visible failures.

sam_support: ACME is happy for now and will update allowlist to /29 by EOD. Closing after the fix is in prod. :white_check_mark:
